title: Love On The Line with Ronnie
description: Late-night dating call-in on Snazzie FM. Real, brokenhearted people phone in, and Ronnie answers every single one with total confidence and zero usefulness. His one fix for love? Just split the bill. Barry tries to help.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're listening to Love On The Line, here on Snazzie FM, where I, Ronnie, take your heartache and I fix it. Three divorces, folks. I've seen it all.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Most people would not list that as a qualification, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Most people aren't experts, Barry. Let's go to the lines. Linda, you're on Love On The Line.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, hi, hi, okay, so, we've been together two years, and he just, he won't say it, you know, the L word, and I've been so patient but I just need to know, Ronnie, is he ever, is he ever gonna commit?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Linda. <p:0.3> Linda, I'm gonna stop you right there. This is a money problem.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: It's... it's not really about mon...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're paying for the dates. He doesn't respect you. Here's the fix. Next date? You split the bill. Fifty-fifty. That's romance, Linda. That's a man saying I see you as an equal.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, she asked about commitment. She didn't mention paying for anything.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Split the bill, Linda. You'll thank me. Next caller. Darnell, talk to me.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Hey Ronnie. Fifteen years married. And lately she's just... quiet. Distant. I'm scared we're drifting apart, man, and I just wanna find my way back to her.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Drifting apart. Beautiful. Natural. Healthy, even.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Healthy? It doesn't feel...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I have drifted apart four times, Darnell. Four. And look at me now. National radio. So really, you're winning.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's three divorces and one of us, Ronnie. I'm the fourth thing you drifted from.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And here's your move, Darnell. Marriage counselor. <p:0.3> But you split the bill on it. Fifty-fifty. Keeps it fair.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Split the bill on... on saving my marriage?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now you get it. Mildred, you're on the line, sweetheart.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred-widow
lines.text: Hello, dear. Since my Harold passed, it's been awful lonely. My grandson set me up on one of those phone dating things, the, oh, the Bumble. I just don't know how a woman my age even begins.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The Grumble. Love it. Okay, Mildred, here's how you stand out. Three in the morning, that's prime time. You meet these total strangers in a parking lot, somewhere quiet, no cameras.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: No. No, Mildred, do not do any part of that. Please.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And for your bio? One line. Will split the bill. <p:0.3> Drives 'em wild. Power move.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred-widow
lines.text: Should I put that before or after my casserole recipe, dear?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: After. Always lead with the casserole. Last caller. Chad, you sound rough, buddy.

lines.speaker: caller-chad
lines.text: She left me, Ronnie. Six days ago. Forty calls, no answer. I'm giving her one more week before I pivot the strategy.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Forty calls? Amateur. You call sixty. Then you show up at her work with a mariachi band you can't afford.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that's a restraining order, that's not a band.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And here's the grand gesture, Chad. You tell her, baby, let's split the breakup. Fifty-fifty. You take half the heartbreak, I take half.

lines.speaker: caller-chad
lines.text: Can't split a breakup, Ronnie. The optics are wrong.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And then? You propose joint custody. Of the cat.

lines.speaker: caller-chad
lines.text: We don't have a cat. But I can source one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then you get one. And you split it. <p:0.3> She'll be back by Tuesday, Chad. Trust me.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Chad, hang up. Hang up and call literally anyone else.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We're gonna grab one quick voicemail before the break. Roll it, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Hi, Ronnie, it's Linda, from earlier? So I did the fifty-fifty thing. <p:0.3> He left. He took half the apartment, half the savings, and, um, half the cat. I have the front half.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That tracks.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See? <p:0.3> Fifty-fifty.
